summary:
H.J. Res. 30 is a joint resolution of congressional disapproval under chapter 8 of title 5, United States Code, the Congressional Review Act. Its sole operative provision provides that Congress disapproves the rule submitted by the Department of Labor entitled “Prudence and Loyalty in Selecting Plan Investments and Exercising Shareholder Rights,” published at 87 Fed. Reg. 73822 on December 1, 2022, and declares that the rule “shall have no force or effect.”

The resolution does not amend any provision of the United States Code, create any new regulatory authority, repeal a statutory provision, authorize appropriations, or make an appropriation. Its operative mechanism is the Congressional Review Act disapproval procedure: if enacted as a joint resolution, the identified Department of Labor rule is nullified pursuant to 5 U.S.C. chapter 8. The text contains no exceptions, conditions precedent beyond enactment, implementation directives, transition rules, savings clauses, deadlines, or separate effective-date provision.
